2.2 Muni Specific Land Use Codes df + QC

Key DFs
 * muni_uc: Muni Specific Land Use Codes from MassGIS, no longer has the muni attached to it
 * muni.df.LUT: from muni_uc, list of munis with documented non-standard LUC
 * muni.diff: list of munis not in muni_uc
 * missing.muni.LUC: list of unique LUC by muni with count of parcels, from raw assessors data
 * std_us.check: join between std_uc and missing.muni.LUC to check if the missing munis have the std LUC in their assessors data
    ? why drop_na() if the muni does not have standard use codes, wouldn't this drop them from check table. That is how the test is set up but if the muni isn't using standard codes we would have lost their unique ones 
```{r}
# QUESTION: Do these 23 municipalities use L3 standardized use codes instead of municipally specific codes?

# Filter full assessors records for missing munis and sum the number of parcels that belong to each code
missing.muni.LUC <- assessors |> filter(CITY %in% muni.diff.list) |> group_by(USE_CODE) |> 
  summarise(
    parcel_num = n()
  ) |> 
  ungroup()

# Join missing muni parcels summed to land use code to the full set of standard use codes.
# full_join() will reveal mismatches with standard use codes.
std_uc.check <- full_join(std_uc, missing.muni.LUC, by = c("STD.USE_CODE" = "USE_CODE")) |> filter(is.na(STD.USE_CODE))

if length(std_uc.check) > 0 {
  print("Munis not in LUT are not using all standard use codes in their assessors data")
  write.csv(
   std_uc.check, 
    here(paste0("04_Output/External/MGIS.LUT_Muni.wo.UniqueCodes_.",q,"_",yr,".csv")),
    row.names = FALSE
  )
} else {
  print("All Land Use Codes used by municipalities not present in the LUT land use code layer use DOR/DLS standard land use codes.")
}


```
Do we have a test for standards codes applied to non-standard descriptions?

# 3.0 Text Analysis Dataframes
# 3.1 One-Digit Unique Land Use Code Terms Dataframes

? Why are filtering out mixed use codes? A: Overlap with other codes

Key Lists:
* od_uc.list: list of unique 1 digit land use codes
* td_uc.list: list of non-mixed use standard 3 digit use codes (intentional?)

Legibility Note:
    You do seem to charnge "td." from meaning 2-digit to 3-digit. I would suggest changing the variable name to td3_uc.list or not creating a 2-digit list at all if it is not used in the analysis.

Key DF
* od_muni.uc[[od_luc]]:  Tables for each one-digit luc group with all the unique muni codes and description in the assessor's data. 
* od_std.uc[[od_luc]]: Tables for each one-digit luc group with all the unique standard codes and description from the LUT.
* td_std.uc[[od_luc]]: lists of uq unique 3 digit standard codes from the LUT, grouped by 1 digit code.
* std.desc_lexicon[[od_luc]]: lists of words in standard descriptions without stop words (whatever those are) 
* std.desc_lexicon_unique[[od_luc]]: unique description words for each one digit land use code, without stop words
* comp_terms_full: all the luc desc from the other LUCs 


Legibility Note: 
    For forloops I like to make the loop variable name more descriptive than i, using "luc" here instead would make it more clear.

# 3.2 Three-Digit Unique Land Use Code Terms Dataframes for Standard Codes
Key DF
* td.std.desc[[td3_luc]]: Tables of unique descriptions for standard 3 digit codes
* td.std.desc_lexicon[[td3_luc]]: Tables of unique words in standard 3 digit code descriptions, without stop words
* td.std.desc_lexicon_unique[[td3_luc]]: Tables of unique words in standard 3 digit code descriptions, without stop words, that are unique to that 3 digit code

# 3.3 Extract Unique Municipal-Specific Land Use Code Terms + Paste Unique Terms into Unique Term List

Key DF/Lists
* od.muni.desc_lexicon[[od_luc]]: Lists of words in municipal-specific code descriptions, without common terms
* od.muni.desc_lexicon_unique[[od_luc]]: Lists of words in municipal-specific code descriptions, without common terms, that are unique to that one digit code

## Legibility Note: 850:883
    This might be cleaner but the casewhen is decently clean

```{r}

gen_muc<-function(prim, sec){
    if(sec %in% c(prim, 0, NA)){
        return(paste0("0", prim, "0"))
    }else{
        return(paste0("0", prim, sec))
    }
}

gen_std_uc<-function(prim, sec){

    return(paste0("Multiple Use (Primarily ", std_uc[od_uc == prim, STD.USE_DESC], " Some ", std_uc[od_uc == sec, STD.USE_DESC], ")"))
}

amended.uc <- unmatched |> 
  mutate(
    MUNI.USE_CODE_fix = case_when(
      mu.flag == FALSE  ~ str_sub(MUNI.USE_CODE, start = 2, end = 4),
      # Residential Mixed Use
      mu.flag == TRUE ~ gen_muc(prim = udef.primary, sec = undef.secondary),
      .default == "hopefully this doesn't happen"
    ),
    STD.USE_DESC = gen_std_uc(prim=udef.primary, sec = undef.secondary)
  )


```

## 4.1.2 Matched

* amended.uc overwritten
    MUNI.USE_CODE_underlying code without a leading 0

    It might  be simpler to do the case_when in this order Lines 1020:1050

```{r}

amended.uc <- matched |> 
  mutate(
    MUNI.USE_CODE_underlying = str_sub(MUNI.USE_CODE, start = 2, end = 4),,
    MUNI.USE_CODE_fix = case_when(
        #description has mixed use terms
      mu.flag == TRUE ~ xwalk_uc,
        #description  does not have mixed use terms or puncutation but does have "unknown" or "other"
      mu.flag == FALSE & td.mu.flag == FALSE & uk.flag == TRUE ~ "000",
        # if there are any puncuation indicators 
      td.mu.flag == TRUE ~ xwalk_uc,
        #if not uknown and doesn't have MU terms or punctiation--fixed underlying LUC
      mu.flag == FALSE ~ MUNI.USE_CODE_underlying,
      .default = "what the hell is going on here?"
    ),
    xwalk_uc = str_sub(MUNI.USE_CODE_fix, start = 1, end = 3)
  )|> 
   select(c(xwalk_uc, MUNI.USE_CODE, MUNI.USE_CODE_fix, MUNI.USE_CODE_underlying, MUNI.USE_DESC, mu.flag, td.mu.flag, muni_name, uk.flag, other, char_count, dls.dupes, matched, initial.use_type))

```

## Actually...
DLS has the 0XX series as "multiple" use not "mixed use". It might be worth reworking all this to be "multiple" except for the residential + commercial since those are what we are generally referring to as mixed use not "the archery center that also has a fishing pond and some of the town forest"

handle_multi_matches<-function(muni, su_tbl){

    muni_su_tbl<-su_tbl%>%
        filter(muni_name = muni)%>%
        rowwise()%>%
        mutate(
            t3_uc_matches = c(str_remove(
                                names(
                                    select(where(
                                    starts_with("flag.") == TRUE))), 
                                "flag.")),
            od_uc_match_idx = match(od_uc, 
                                    str_sub(t3_uc_matches, start = 1, end = 1)),
            STD.USE_CODE_comp = t3_uc_matches[od_uc_match_idx]
            )
}

# Remove various helper variables from the amend_tbl dataframe.
matched_amend_tbl_clean <- matched_amend_tbl |> 
  # Remove Helper Variables
  select(!starts_with("flag.")) |> 
  select(-c(od_uc, numTRUE, mxu.flag, mxu.td.flag, uk, dls.dupes, su.amend.flag, UCID)) |> 
  select(-c(STD.USE_DESC)) |> 
  # Join standard land use code descriptions back into the data.
  left_join(
    std_uc,
    by = c("STD.USE_CODE")
  ) |> 
  select(-c(xwalk_uc.x, xwalk_uc.y, od_uc, td_uc)) |> 
  # Create placeholder for MUNI.USE_CODE_underlying for single use codes.
  mutate(
    MUNI.USE_CODE_underlying = "single use",
    comparison = if_else(STD.USE_CODE == STD.USE_CODE_comp, 1, 0)
  ) |>  
  # Move around the variables
  relocate(
    STD.USE_CODE,
    STD.USE_DESC,
    MUNI.USE_CODE,
    MUNI.USE_DESC,
    MUNI.USE_CODE_underlying,
    muni_name
  )

# Clean up the environment.
gc()
# MIXED USE CODE ASSIGNMENT
mxu.matched_amend_tbl <- matched.amend_mxu |> ungroup() |>
  mutate(
      # Creates a variable that represents what the municipality believes to be the primary use based on the 1-9 one-digit use code categories present in the L3 Stanardized Use Code codebook.
    undef.primary = str_sub(MUNI.USE_CODE, start = 1, end = 1),
      # Creates a variable that represents what the municipality believes to be the secondary use based on the 1-9 one-digit use code categories present in the L3 Stanardized Use Code codebook.
    undef.secondary = str_sub(MUNI.USE_CODE, start = 2, end = 2),
    STD.USE_CODE_comp = case_when(
      # Residential Mixed Use
      undef.primary == 1 & undef.secondary %in% c(2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9) ~ paste0("0",undef.primary,undef.secondary),
      undef.primary == 1 & undef.secondary %in% c(1,0,NA) ~ "010",
      # Open Space Mixed Use
      undef.primary == 2 & undef.secondary %in% c(1,3,4,5,6,7,8,9) ~ paste0("0",undef.primary,undef.secondary),
      undef.primary == 2 & undef.secondary %in% c(2,0,NA) ~ "020",
      # Commercial Mixed Use
      undef.primary == 3 & undef.secondary %in% c(1,2,4,5,6,7,8,9) ~ paste0("0",undef.primary,undef.secondary),
      undef.primary == 3 & undef.secondary %in% c(3,0,NA) ~ "030",
      # Industrial Mixed Use
      undef.primary == 4 & undef.secondary %in% c(1,2,3,5,6,7,8,9) ~ paste0("0",undef.primary,undef.secondary),
      undef.primary == 4 & undef.secondary %in% c(4,0,NA) ~ "040",
      # Private Property Mixed Use
      undef.primary == 5 & undef.secondary %in% c(1,2,3,4,6,7,8,9) ~ paste0("0",undef.primary,undef.secondary),
      undef.primary == 5 & undef.secondary %in% c(5,0,NA) ~ "050",
      # Forest Mixed Use
      undef.primary == 6 & undef.secondary %in% c(1,2,3,4,5,7,8,9) ~ paste0("0",undef.primary,undef.secondary),
      undef.primary == 6 & undef.secondary %in% c(6,0,NA) ~ "060",
      # Agriculture Mixed Use
      undef.primary == 7 & undef.secondary %in% c(1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9) ~ paste0("0",undef.primary,undef.secondary),
      undef.primary == 7 & undef.secondary %in% c(7,0,NA) ~ "070",
      # Recreation Mixed Use
      undef.primary == 8 & undef.secondary %in% c(1,2,3,4,5,6,7,9) ~ paste0("0",undef.primary,undef.secondary),
      undef.primary == 8 & undef.secondary %in% c(8,0,NA) ~ "080",
      # Exempt Mixed Use
      undef.primary == 9 & undef.secondary %in% c(1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8) ~ paste0("0",undef.primary,undef.secondary),
      undef.primary == 9 & undef.secondary %in% c(9,0,NA) ~ "090",
      # uh....
      .default = "what the hell is going on here?"
    ),
     STD.USE_DESC_comp = case_when(
      STD.USE_CODE == "000" ~ "Use code not known or nor provided.",
      STD.USE_CODE == "010" ~ "Mixed Use (Primarily Residential, Some Other)",
      STD.USE_CODE == "012" ~ "Mixed Use (Primarily Residential, Some Open Space)",
      STD.USE_CODE == "013" ~ "Mixed Use (Primarily Residential, Some Commercial)",
      STD.USE_CODE == "014" ~ "Mixed Use (Primarily Residential, Some Industrial)",
      STD.USE_CODE == "015" ~ "Mixed Use (Primarily Residential, Some Private Property)",
      STD.USE_CODE == "016" ~ "Mixed Use (Primarily Residential, Some Forest)",
      STD.USE_CODE == "017" ~ "Mixed Use (Primarily Residential, Some Agriculture)",
      STD.USE_CODE == "018" ~ "Mixed Use (Primarily Residential, Some Recreation)",
      STD.USE_CODE == "019" ~ "Mixed Use (Primarily Residential, Some Exempt)",
      STD.USE_CODE == "020" ~ "Mixed Use (Primarily Open Space, Some Other)",
      STD.USE_CODE == "023" ~ "Mixed Use (Primarily Open Space, Commercial)",
      STD.USE_CODE == "030" ~ "Mixed Use (Primarily Commercial, Some Other)",
      STD.USE_CODE == "032" ~ "Mixed Use (Primarily Commercial, Some Open Space)",
      STD.USE_CODE == "035" ~ "Mixed Use (Primarily Commercial, Some Private Property)",
      STD.USE_CODE == "039" ~ "Mixed Use (Primarily Commercial, Some Exempt)",
      STD.USE_CODE == "040" ~ "Mixed Use (Primarily Industrial, Some Other)",
      STD.USE_CODE == "042" ~ "Mixed Use (Primarily Industrial, Some Open Space)",
      STD.USE_CODE == "045" ~ "Mixed Use (Primarily Industrial, Some Private Property)",
      STD.USE_CODE == "049" ~ "Mixed Use (Primarily Industrial, Some Exempt)",
      STD.USE_CODE == "050" ~ "Mixed Use (Primarily Private Property, Some Other)",
      STD.USE_CODE == "060" ~ "Mixed Use (Primarily Forest, Some Other)",
      STD.USE_CODE == "070" ~ "Mixed Use (Primarily Agriculture, Some Other)",
      STD.USE_CODE == "072" ~ "Mixed Use (Primarily Agriculture, Some Open Space)",
      STD.USE_CODE == "080" ~ "Mixed Use (Primarily Recreation, Some Other)",
      STD.USE_CODE == "089" ~ "Mixed Use (Primarily Recreation, Some Exempt)",
      STD.USE_CODE == "090" ~ "Mixed Use (Primarily Exempt, Some Other)",
      STD.USE_CODE == "091" ~ "Mixed Use (Primarily Exempt, Some Residential)",
      STD.USE_CODE == "092" ~ "Mixed Use (Primarily Exempt, Some Open Space)",
      STD.USE_CODE == "093" ~ "Mixed Use (Primarily Exempt, Some Commercial)",
      STD.USE_CODE == "094" ~ "Mixed Use (Primarily Exempt, Some Industrial)",
      STD.USE_CODE == "095" ~ "Mixed Use (Primarily Exempt, Some Private Property)",
      STD.USE_CODE == "096" ~ "Mixed Use (Primarily Exempt, Some Forest)",
      STD.USE_CODE == "097" ~ "Mixed Use (Primarily Exempt, Some Agriculture)",
      STD.USE_CODE == "098" ~ "Mixed Use (Primarily Exempt, Some Recreation)",
      .default = STD.USE_DESC
     ),
    # Create a stand in for the MUNI.USE_CODE_underlying variable. No useful information is stored in the three digit code municipalities assigned to these mixed use codes.
    MUNI.USE_CODE_underlying = "single use",
    comparison = if_else(STD.USE_CODE == STD.USE_CODE_comp, 1, 0)
  ) |> 
  select(c(STD.USE_CODE, STD.USE_DESC, STD.USE_CODE_comp, MUNI.USE_CODE, MUNI.USE_DESC, muni_name, mxu.amend.flag, comparison))


#~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
# Create a single dataframe for the single use amended land use code crosswalk
matched_su.luc_xwalk <- bind_rows(matched_amend_tbl_clean, mxu.matched_amend_tbl) |> 
  mutate(
    STD.USE_CODE = if_else(MUNI.USE_DESC %in% in.need.of.use_code, "001", STD.USE_CODE),
    STD.USE_DESC = if_else(MUNI.USE_DESC %in% in.need.of.use_code, "Flag for DLS/BLA Code Update.", STD.USE_DESC)
  )

ta_comp_tbl <- matched_su.luc_xwalk |> 
  group_by(mxu.amend.flag, comparison) |> 
  summarize(
    n_codes = n()
  ) |> 
  ungroup()

# Save the single use amended land use code crosswalk
# As csv
write.csv(
  matched_su.luc_xwalk,
  here(paste0("04_Output/Internal/matched_su.amended_xwalk_.",q,"_",yr,".csv")),
  row.names = FALSE
)

# As RDS
write_rds(matched_su.luc_xwalk, here(paste0("04_Output/Internal/matched_su.amended_xwalk_.",q,"_",yr,".rds")))

# Environment Cleanup
gc()
